headline: GAAP loss deepens on occupancy declines, FFO holds steady
summary_short: Alexandria reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $662.8 million, down 13.0% y/y, and a GAAP net loss attributable to common stockholders of $0.43 per diluted share, while FFO per share - diluted, as adjusted, was $1.73.
summary_long: Revenue fell 13.0% y/y to $662.8 million and 1.2% sequentially, as same-property NOI declined 10.6% on lower occupancy from previously disclosed lease expirations. The company posted a GAAP net loss attributable to common stockholders of $72.8 million (-$0.43/share diluted), narrower than the year-ago loss but a swing from a $361.7 million profit last quarter. FFO per share - diluted, as adjusted -- the REIT industry's non-GAAP measure -- was $1.73 for the quarter and $3.46 for 1H26. Cash fell to $470.4 million and long-term debt to $12.81 billion, both down y/y. Alexandria narrowed full-year 2026 FFO-per-share guidance to $6.35-$6.45 (midpoint $6.40, unchanged), and held its 4Q26 net-debt-to-EBITDA target of 5.6x-6.2x.
confidence_notes: Alexandria is a REIT: GAAP EPS is heavily affected by real estate depreciation and gain/loss items and diverges materially from FFO per share, the metric the company and sector emphasize -- both are reported as-disclosed above, not reconciled to each other. The q/q comparison for net income/EPS reflects a swing from a large prior-quarter GAAP gain to this quarter's loss; the prior-quarter figure was not investigated for one-time items beyond what the release itself notes.

drivers.explanation: Same-property NOI fell 10.6% in Q2, driven by lower occupancy from previously disclosed lease expirations with downtime (657,492 RSF in Q1, 260,888 RSF in Q2).
Full-year FFO-per-share guidance midpoint held at $6.40 as an expected benefit from later dispositions offsets higher interest expense and lower capitalized interest.
